facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October. This burnout is related to his work as a project manager.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October.

facts.heading: Work loss caused burnout
facts.content: Daniel's burnout resulted from losing a big client. Half of his team moved to a rescue plan.
facts.evidence: We lost a big client, half of our team moved onto the rescue plan

facts.heading: Managing multiple jobs
facts.content: Daniel ended up doing three people's jobs after the client loss. These people never came back.
facts.evidence: so I ended up doing three people's jobs. Just never came back after that.

facts.heading: Late night work habits
facts.content: Daniel works late, answering messages at 10 at night. He is still thinking about work.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 at night. I'm not working and thinking about work.

facts.heading: Poor sleep quality
facts.content: Daniel's sleep is terrible, averaging about four hours per night. He wakes up at three in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours. I wake up at three in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Work schedule impacts sleep
facts.content: When Daniel wakes at three, he has to start shipping schedules. He then calculates how little sleep he will get, which makes it worse.
facts.evidence: We have to start shipping schedules, the client, whether or not I've forgotten something. Then I look at the clock and I do the math on how little sleep I'm gonna get, which makes it worse.

facts.heading: Father's Parkinson's diagnosis
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn. This diagnosis is a significant factor in Daniel's life.
facts.evidence: His diagnosis was Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's current condition
facts.content: Daniel's father's handshake is slower, he gets frustrated, and he is having a drink. He is often distraught.
facts.evidence: His handshake is slower, he gets frustrated, he's having a drink and he's always being distraught when.

facts.heading: Daniel manages father's care
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds for neurology appointments every few weeks. The travel time is about an hour each way.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks, it's about an hour each way.

facts.heading: Sister lives in Toronto
facts.content: Daniel's younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto. All care for their father falls on Daniel.
facts.evidence: My younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto so all the care for our father falls on me.

facts.heading: Guilt about sharing feelings
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for saying he is tired. He feels his father feels selfish to be tired when he is ill.
facts.evidence: Guilty for even saying it. He feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill.

facts.heading: Daniel avoids telling sister
facts.content: Daniel does not say anything to Hannah about his feelings. He says fine when she asks how he is.
facts.evidence: So I don't say anything to anyone. She calls him every Sunday. She asks how I am, and I say fine.

facts.heading: Avoidance of facing issues
facts.content: Daniel cannot face something. He breathes and looks at people going in.
facts.evidence: because I can't face it. That's an important thing to notice.

facts.heading: GP visit results
facts.content: Daniel had blood tests done by his GP. The results were normal.
facts.evidence: She had blood tests. They were all normal.

facts.heading: GP suggestion for support
facts.content: Daniel asked his GP about talking to someone. The GP said he had not got the time.
facts.evidence: I ask about talking to someone, they said I hadn't got the time.

facts.heading: Girlfriend Claire's patience
facts.content: Claire is very patient with Daniel. She makes him tea and does not push him to talk.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire's behavior change
facts.content: Claire stopped asking if Daniel wanted to go away for the weekend. Daniel always said no.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.

facts.heading: Emails prevent rest
facts.content: The emails prevent Daniel from resting. He has to return to 200 emails if he is away.
facts.evidence: If I'm away, I'll come back to 200 of them.

facts.heading: Rest has a price
facts.content: Daniel feels that even rest has a price. He cannot remember the last time he was properly off.
facts.evidence: So even rest has a price? Yeah, exactly. Can't remember the last time I was properly off.

facts.heading: Stopped running activity
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago. He has not gone back.
facts.evidence: It stopped about two months ago. My legs feel like, like, loud. And I just never went back.

facts.heading: Loss of self from running
facts.content: Daniel feels like he has lost a part of himself. He describes the running as being a time when nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: Like, I've lost a part of myself. It was still one time in the week, nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Boss's demanding communication
facts.content: Daniel's boss sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.
facts.evidence: Pearson. He's alright as a person, but he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that the company might let him go due to a restructuring in the spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Fear of negative reaction
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that his boss will think he is not coming at it if he does not answer.
facts.evidence: Dunn, he'd think I wasn't come at it.

facts.heading: Mixed feelings about job loss
facts.content: Daniel thinks part of him would be relieved if he were let go, but he would feel horrible about being relieved.
facts.evidence: You'd think part of me would be relieved. I'd feel horrible about being relieved.

facts.heading: Irritability and physical symptoms
facts.content: Daniel feels a lot of tiredness and irritability. He experienced shaking hands during a brief interaction at the toilet.
facts.evidence: A lot mostly. And irritable. It's like to the colleague last week or nothing in one tenths at the toilet for ten minutes. Hurry was going and my hand was shaking.

facts.heading: Fright happened on train
facts.content: Daniel has experienced frightening episodes a couple of times. This happened once on a train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: couple of times. Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform.

facts.heading: Coping with fright
facts.content: Daniel uses blusing to cope with fright. He ends up coping after the event.
facts.evidence: They're blusing it. Then I end up like, I don't know, coping.

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habit
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day. He started having wine in the evenings to switch his head off.
facts.evidence: I went about six cups a day and I started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off, to glasses, sometimes tree.

facts.heading: Drinking wine for sleep
facts.content: Daniel drinks wine in the evenings to try and switch his head off. He feels the wine works for an hour.
facts.evidence: to glasses, sometimes tree. How do you feel about the vine? Easy. It works for an hour.

facts.heading: Waking up three times
facts.content: Daniel wakes up three times during the night. He knows the wine is not helping.
facts.evidence: I wake up three anyway. I know it's not helping.

facts.heading: Feeling of listing problems
facts.content: Daniel feels like he is listing everything wrong with him. He hears a person holding a great deal on his own.
facts.evidence: It feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me. I hear a person who has been holding a great deal on his own for a long time.

facts.heading: Caring for the nights
facts.content: Daniel thinks that if he could sleep, he could probably cope with the rest.
facts.evidence: If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Grandfather's behavior
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather worked at the mines in the orchard. He never complained about anything.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked at the mines in the orchard. He never complained about anything.

facts.heading: Grandfather's coping style
facts.content: Daniel observed that his grandfather would just get on with it.
facts.evidence: Just get on with it. And you? I'm the same.

facts.heading: Feeling about self-identity
facts.content: Daniel stated he is not weak. He is just very tired. He is unsure if he believes this yet.
facts.evidence: That I'm not Week. I'm just very tired. Maybe. I don't know if I believe it yet.

facts.heading: Proposed small change
facts.content: Daniel was asked to try something small between now and next week. He agreed to try turning off his phone for 20 minutes in the evening.
facts.evidence: Would you be willing to try something small? I can't tell small. I can't go much left. Very small. Fix time in the evening when you switch off your phone even for 20 minutes.

facts.heading: Plan for tracking sleep
facts.content: Daniel agreed to write down when he wakes up if he wakes up.
facts.evidence: I can do that. Write down when I wake up, if I wake up.

facts.heading: Current feeling after session
facts.content: Daniel felt lighter after discussing things. He felt shaky but normal.
facts.evidence: Darn, but lighter. It's normal to feel a bit shaky after saying all that. Very normal.

facts.heading: Agreed to meet next week
facts.content: Daniel agreed to meet again the following week.
facts.evidence: Same time next week? Yeah, I'll be here.
